title: When the Veil Sings
premise: Vesper Halloran, a mercenary bound by oath to the silent god Veil, has spent years running contraband through the Thornfell mountains while pretending her divine mark is just a scar. When the border wards collapse and every star vanishes in a single night, she learns the god's silence was no abandonment: the court beneath the mountain has been devouring its voice, one stolen soul at a time—and the newest soul is her sworn brother Tam, sold to pay a debt she unknowingly inherited from her mother. To reach the Undercourt before his soul is fully consumed, Vesper must ally with Sable, an exiled Undercourt noble who once loved her mother and now offers dangerous truths about Vesper's inheritance. Torn between loyalty to her mercenary company, who want her to flee, and the truth that her bloodline was the price of the wards' original binding, Vesper descends into the mountain. In the climax she discovers she can restore the god only by surrendering her own soul—but she instead rewrites the old bargain, offering the court her inheritance of memory rather than her self, freeing Tam, reigniting the stars, and leaving her marked forever as the Veil's new living voice.
about_author: Paloma Blackwood is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent six years mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction, a trade that left her with a lifelong obsession with borders and the things that cross them. She writes fantasy from a stone farmhouse where, she insists, the walls hum on windy nights.

chapters.title: The God Who Stopped Answering
chapters.summary: Vesper guides a smuggler's caravan through Thornfell's passes, trading wry banter with her sworn brother Tam while hiding the dead silence of her divine mark. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: comfortable routine shadowed by quiet grief—she prays nightly to a god that hasn't spoken in three years.

chapters.title: Salt for the Border Wards
chapters.summary: At the fortified town of Greyhollow, Vesper bribes a ward-keeper and notices the wards flickering like guttering candles. A stranger, Sable, watches her with unsettling recognition. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: first unease—the world's machinery is failing, and someone knows her name.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Every star goes out at once; the border wards shatter like glass. In the panic, Tam confesses he signed a debt-contract with brokers of the Undercourt to cover the company's losses. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into guilt—her brother sold himself because of debts tied to her.

chapters.title: What the Company Owes
chapters.summary: The mercenary company votes to scatter and hide; their captain, Brannoc, orders Vesper to burn her mark and vanish. She refuses, and they part badly. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: loyalty tested—choosing Tam over the only family she has left.

chapters.title: Sable of the Deep Court
chapters.summary: Sable intercepts Vesper on the road, revealing she is exiled nobility of the court beneath the mountain and knew Vesper's mother, Maerin, who brokered the original ward-binding. POV: alternating Vesper/Sable. Emotional beat: wary fascination—every answer Sable gives costs something.

chapters.title: Maerin's Ledger
chapters.summary: In her mother's hidden cache, Vesper finds a ledger showing the wards were paid for with a generational debt: one soul per generation from the Halloran line. Her name is next after Tam's collateral. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: betrayal across generations—inheritance as a trap.

chapters.title: The Hollow Pilgrims
chapters.summary: Traveling toward the mountain, Vesper and Sable pass villages of 'hollowed' people—soul-shorn laborers the Undercourt leases back to the surface. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: horror made ordinary; the cost of the peace she grew up under.

chapters.title: Brannoc's Blade
chapters.summary: Brannoc catches up, not to apologize but to drag Vesper home before the company's creditors learn a Halloran still lives. They duel; she wins but spares him. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: love against duty inverted—he serves duty, she chooses love, and both bleed for it.

chapters.title: The Singing Cave
chapters.summary: Sheltering in a cave, Vesper hears the silent god for the first time in years—a faint song leaking up from below. The mark on her arm warms. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: fragile hope—the god isn't dead, it's imprisoned.

chapters.title: Gate of Teeth
chapters.summary: Sable leads Vesper to the Undercourt's gate, a canyon mouth ringed with petrified petitioners. To enter, Vesper must declare her lineage aloud, making her claim—and her debt—public. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: point of no return; speaking truth as an act of courage.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Descending through bioluminescent vaults, Vesper witnesses the Undercourt's splendor built on harvested souls, including flickers of Tam already fading in the soul-vats. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: awe curdling to rage.

chapters.title: Audience with the Regent
chapters.summary: The Regent, wearing a crown of fused starlight, offers Vesper a deal: Tam's freedom in exchange for her willing surrender as the final payment closing Maerin's contract. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: temptation—duty dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Sable's Treason
chapters.summary: Sable is exposed as having guided Vesper down not to save Tam but to trigger a succession crisis that could restore her own house. Vesper is thrown in the cells beside what remains of Tam. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: betrayal upon betrayal; trust shattered.

chapters.title: Tam, Half-Gone
chapters.summary: In the dark, Vesper speaks to the hollowing Tam, using shared memories to anchor him. He tells her the Regent fears the Veil's return more than any debtor. POV: Tam (first time). Emotional beat: tenderness as resistance; loyalty as lifeline.

chapters.title: The Regent's Secret
chapters.summary: A sympathetic hollowed servant reveals the Regent devoured the Veil's voice to seize the wards' power, but the stolen song is tearing the Regent apart—the stars went out because the crown is cracking. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the enemy is dying and desperate, therefore most dangerous.

chapters.title: Riot of the Hollowed
chapters.summary: Vesper sparks a revolt among the soul-shorn laborers by singing a fragment of the Veil's song, which briefly restores the crowd's selves. Chaos spreads through the vaults. POV: alternating Vesper/Tam. Emotional beat: collective hope igniting; her voice matters.

chapters.title: Sable's Choice
chapters.summary: Cornered during the riot, Sable must choose between her house's restoration and helping Vesper; she opens the soul-vault and confesses she loved Maerin, and failed her. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: redemption purchased with ruin.

chapters.title: The Crown of Cracked Stars
chapters.summary: Vesper confronts the Regent atop the soul-vats. The Regent offers her everything—Tam, power, absolution—if she takes the cracking crown herself. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the climax's true temptation: becoming the monster to end the monster.

chapters.title: The Bargain Rewritten
chapters.summary: Refusing both crown and sacrifice, Vesper invokes her inheritance differently: she offers the court her memories of Maerin and the original contract, dissolving the generational debt and unbinding the stolen voices. The Regent unravels as the song leaves the crown. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: triumph through refusal—truth outbidding duty.

chapters.title: The Veil Sings
chapters.summary: Freed souls stream upward as the Veil's full song floods the mountain; the stars reignite over Thornfell. Tam wakes whole; Sable stays below to help rebuild a court without a devourer. POV: alternating Vesper/Tam. Emotional beat: catharsis—grief transmuted into music.

chapters.title: Marked
chapters.summary: On the surface, Vesper finds the company waiting at Greyhollow. Brannoc kneels—not to a god, but to her choice. Her mark now glows with the god's living voice, audible whenever she sings. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: reconciliation; family remade by honesty.

chapters.title: Roads Still Worth Walking
chapters.summary: Months later, Vesser walks the passes as the Veil's herald, smuggling nothing but news and songs, with Tam at her side and letters from Sable arriving by strange couriers. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—an inheritance finally chosen, not suffered.
